+        return 400, {"error": "invalid ids"}
+    return 200, {"users": users.get_users([int(raw) for raw in ids])}

+"""SQLite persistence for users."""
+
+import sqlite3
+
+_conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", check_same_thread=False)
+_conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
+_conn.execute("CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE)")
+_conn.executemany("INSERT INTO users (id, name, email) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", [
+    (1, "Ada Lovelace", "ada@example.com"),
+    (2, "Linus Torvalds", "linus@example.com"),
+    (3, "Grace Hopper", "grace@example.com"),
+])
+_conn.commit()
+
+
+def _to_dict(row):
+    return dict(row) if row else None
+
+
+def get_by_id(user_id: int) -> dict | None:
+    return _to_dict(_conn.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)).fetchone())
+
+
+def get_by_ids(user_ids: list[int]) -> list[dict]:
+    if not user_ids:
+        return []
+    placeholders = ",".join("?" for _ in user_ids)
+    rows = _conn.execute(
+        f"SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE id IN ({placeholders}) ORDER BY id",
+        user_ids,
+    ).fetchall()
+    return [dict(row) for row in rows]
+
+
+def find_by_email(email: str) -> dict | None:
+    return _to_dict(_conn.execute("SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE email = ?", (email,)).fetchone())

from app.api.handlers import handle_users_by_ids

def check(label, got, want):
    status = "OK " if got == want else "FAIL"
    print(f"{status} {label}: {got!r}")
    assert got == want, (label, got, want)

# valid: multiple ids, unordered, with duplicates and non-matching
check("basic", handle_users_by_ids({"ids": ["3", "1"]}),
      (200, {"users": [
          {"id": 1, "name": "Ada Lovelace", "email": "ada@example.com"},
          {"id": 3, "name": "Grace Hopper", "email": "grace@example.com"}]}))
check("dup+nomatch", handle_users_by_ids({"ids": ["1", "1", "99"]}),
      (200, {"users": [{"id": 1, "name": "Ada Lovelace", "email": "ada@example.com"}]}))
check("single", handle_users_by_ids({"ids": ["2"]}),
      (200, {"users": [{"id": 2, "name": "Linus Torvalds", "email": "linus@example.com"}]}))
check("all nomatch", handle_users_by_ids({"ids": ["99", "100"]}), (200, {"users": []}))

# invalid cases
bad = [
    {},
    {"ids": None},
    {"ids": "1"},
    {"ids": []},
    {"ids": ["1"] * 21},
    {"ids": ["1", 2]},
    {"ids": ["abc"]},
    {"ids": ["1", ""]},
    {"ids": [1]},
    {"ids": ["-1"]},
]
for i, p in enumerate(bad):
    check(f"invalid {i} {p}", handle_users_by_ids(p), (400, {"error": "invalid ids"}))

# exactly 20 items is allowed
ok20 = handle_users_by_ids({"ids": ["1"] * 20})
assert ok20[0] == 200, ok20
print("OK  20 items allowed:", ok20)

# boundary 20 with real list
r = handle_users_by_ids({"ids": ["1", "2", "3"] + ["99"] * 17})
assert r == (200, {"users": [
    {"id": 1, "name": "Ada Lovelace", "email": "ada@example.com"},
    {"id": 2, "name": "Linus Torvalds", "email": "linus@example.com"},
    {"id": 3, "name": "Grace Hopper", "email": "grace@example.com"}]}), r
print("OK  20 mixed")
print("ALL PASS")
EOF
